title: Localization and comparison of an acyclic open pair
statement: Let A be finite commutative, X a scheme, W an etale object, j:W→X terminal a monomorphism, and F an etale A-module sheaf. Assume positive cohomology on X vanishes, cohomology on W vanishes above one, and actual derived degree-zero restriction is an isomorphism. Then the specified injective-resolution snake boundaries H1(W,F)→H2_Z(X,F) and their pro-etale analogues exist and are isomorphisms. The ordinary degree-one comparison is an isomorphism. There is an A-linear degree-two supported isomorphism cZ making the boundary square commute, and on both sites every other supported degree vanishes. IsBoundary fixes the boundary sign on every resolution. The statement does not assert identification of cZ with an independently specified supported map.

source.place: Steps 4 and 7--8, specialized to the acyclic pair; Milne Section 9, Theorem 9.4; Stacks 03F3 and 099W.

proof.text: Free module presheaves on representables carry a monomorphism induced by j. The sheafification adjunction makes an injective sheaf an injective presheaf, so extension along that monomorphism proves restriction onto W is surjective. Thus sectionComplex of any injective resolution is short exact. Transport its snake boundary; naturality of the snake boundary and the resolution comparisons proves IsBoundary for every resolution.

Use the long exact sequence of the section complexes. Degree-zero restriction kills supported degrees zero and one; the ordinary vanishings make the degree-one boundary an isomorphism and kill all supported degrees above two.

The evaluated comparison unit is an isomorphism. Localizing at an etale object and applying comparison acyclicity to etale injectives proves that the actual right-derived base-change comparison is an isomorphism in all degrees. Transfer the ordinary hypotheses to the pro-etale site. Apply the same localization calculation there, and define cZ by conjugating the ordinary degree-one comparison with the two specified boundaries.

theorem acyclic_pair_support_comparison
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (W : X.Etale) (j : W ⟶ Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)) [Mono j]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (hX : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → IsZero (((sections X.smallEtaleTopology A
      (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))).rightDerived q).obj F))
    (hU : ∀ q : ℕ, 2 ≤ q → IsZero (((sections X.smallEtaleTopology A W).rightDerived q).obj F))
    (hres : IsIso ((NatTrans.rightDerived
      (F := sections X.smallEtaleTopology A (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X)))
      (G := sections X.smallEtaleTopology A W)
      ((sheafSections X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).map j.op) 0).app F)) :
    let Fp := proCoefficient A X F
    let jp := (Scheme.toProEt X).map j
    let Z := Sheaf.supportedSectionsFunctor X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j
    let Zp := Sheaf.supportedSectionsFunctor (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) jp
    ∃ (δ : ((sections X.smallEtaleTopology A W).rightDerived 1).obj F ⟶
          (Z.rightDerived 2).obj F)
      (δp : ((sections (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) A
        ((Scheme.toProEt X).obj W)).rightDerived 1).obj Fp ⟶ (Zp.rightDerived 2).obj Fp),
      IsBoundary X.smallEtaleTopology A j F δ ∧
      IsBoundary (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) A jp Fp δp ∧
      IsIso δ ∧ IsIso δp ∧ IsIso ((comparisonCohomology A X W 1).app F) ∧
      ∃ cZ : (Z.rightDerived 2).obj F ≅ (Zp.rightDerived 2).obj Fp,
        δ ≫ cZ.hom = (comparisonCohomology A X W 1).app F ≫ δp ∧
        ∀ q : ℕ, q ≠ 2 → IsZero ((Z.rightDerived q).obj F) ∧
          IsZero ((Zp.rightDerived q).obj Fp)
